roles.title: Regression test
roles.mission: Write a test that reproduces the problem first
roles.brief: Read the problem description at the end of the README, then the project's README, `package.json` (or another build file) and directories, and work out how it runs and which endpoint, page or function the problem is in; if the problem involves a company rule, look up the original in the knowledge base source "Larkspur Outfitters" (the standards listed in the task). Write one test that reproduces it, `tests/regress-<topic>.test.js` (`node:test`; module style as the project uses; if the project is not written in JavaScript, have the test run the project's own command with `node:child_process` to reproduce it), with a test name that starts with `AC-1:` and says what the correct behaviour is. It should be red now: run `node --test tests/regress-<topic>.test.js` to confirm that it is red and that it runs. Do not change code.

roles.title: Fix
roles.mission: Find the cause and fix it with the smallest change
roles.brief: Read the problem description and the regression test `tests/regress-*.test.js`, find the cause and fix it with the smallest change, with no refactoring on the side; where a company rule is involved, change the code as the knowledge base original says and put the rule ID in the commit message. Tests belong to the person who wrote them: you change nothing under `tests/`. When you are done, run the regression test and the project's existing tests (`npm test`, or `node --test "tests/**/*.test.js"` if there is none): the regression test must turn green, and nothing that was green may turn red. If you think the test itself is wrong, do not bend the code to fit it: say why in your summary.
